title: Beathag Dhubh asks for the order at Cnoc fhiadhaich
summary: Beathag Dhubh, custodian of Doire mhòr, goes down to the washing-floors at Cnoc fhiadhaich with the carter Seònaid Bhàn and asks the agent Amos Tanner to show her the order that took her village's stream. He has none. The washing needs water, he says, and the stream goes with the working; a complaint may be written and sent on to Ros dhomhain.

title: Doire mhòr carries its water from the cattle spring
summary: With the stream penned behind the washing gang's bank, the households of Doire mhòr carry their water by yoke and pail from the cattle spring at the foot of the brae, the better part of a mile each way. Beathag Dhubh's roll names every household that carries, and among the carriers is Tormod, son of Ruairidh.

title: Beathag Dhubh's letter to the council entered
summary: The custodian of Doire mhòr writes to Comhairle a' Chùraim at Cathair dhearg of the taking of Doire mhòr's stream. Seònaid Bhàn carries the letter down the road in her cart and puts it into the hand of a custodians' clerk. The council enters it in its roll, and the stream is not let go that season.

title: The store at Àth ìseal takes no barter
summary: In the hungry autumn the store of A' Chompanaidh at Àth ìseal sells meal to the hill villages over its counter for marks only. Its clerk refuses cheese, wool and a woman's bronze brooch, having no book for them, and the women of the villages send their men back to the pits for coin.

title: Gormshuil nic Fhearchair dies at Cathair dhearg
summary: Gormshuil nic Fhearchair dies at Cathair dhearg in the last days of an t-Sultain, in her seventy-first year. She had kept the council's list of the island's words since the ships came, refused to sign Puingean a' Chalaidh, and learned the humans' letters in her old age.

title: Muireall carries Gormshuil's papers to the loft at Muileann chaol
summary: Muireall nic Fhearchair drives her aunt Gormshuil's papers east in a hired pony-cart to the loft of Beathag nic Thòmais at Muileann chaol, away from the reach of Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir. Held by rain at Cuan chrom, she reads Clàr nan Dà Fhichead Dath aloud to the carter Seònaid Bhàn.

title: The meal-carts of Doire fhiadhaich lodged at Cuan chrom
summary: Nine ox-carts of meal from the villages of Doire fhiadhaich, sent north to the hungry hills under Lagh a' Bhìdh Roinnte, reach the ford at Cuan chrom in the rain of an Dàmhair. The carter of Cuan chrom, Seònaid Bhàn's father, takes their drivers and oxen into his own house and byre for the night.

title: Seven carts give their meal at the village doors
summary: Of the nine meal-carts from Doire fhiadhaich, the seven that refuse the agents' marks at Àth ìseal go on into the hills and give their meal away sack by sack at the doors of the hill villages, as Lagh a' Bhìdh Roinnte bids. Their drivers come home by the carriers' road with empty carts.

title: The first households leave Doire mhòr
summary: In the second summer of the carrying the first households of Doire mhòr leave the village. Most go down to the timber huts at Àth ìseal, others to Muileann chrom or the capital. Tormod, who had carried water up for two summers, goes down to Àth ìseal with the rest. Beathag Dhubh stays.

title: The shrine-stone of Cidhe Beag set under a rowan
summary: When the canoe landing at Cidhe Beag is widened into a coal quay, the old ferryman of the landing chooses a new place for its shrine-stone on the bank above, under a rowan within sight of the water. Four masons carry it up on a hurdle, and the ferryman puts meal in its hollow.

title: The last salmon netted at the green river's mouth
summary: The fishermen of Ceann leathan net the last salmon taken at the mouth of the Abhainn uaine, a small hen fish found empty of eggs. The next spring no fish come in from the sea, the gravel of their spawning grounds lying under the grey slurry from the washing-floors.

title: Seònaid Bhàn marries Pàdraig mac Artair
summary: Seònaid Bhàn, carter of Cuan chrom, marries Pàdraig mac Artair, a carter of Doire chaol. They live in her father's house at Cuan chrom beside the roofless carters' house at the quay, and their son Murchadh is born there the next winter.

title: Seònaid Bhàn takes the old carters' house at Cuan chrom
summary: The custodians of Cuan chrom let the roofless carters' house at their quay to Seònaid Bhàn for a rent of one cheese a year. Twenty carters of Doire chaol give a week's work each towards the new roof for a year's lodging at half price, and its timber comes up from Doire fhiadhaich.

title: Seònaid's rule of marks and barter
summary: On the first night of An Taigh-seinnse Mòr Seònaid Bhàn takes a hill carter's cheese and fleece for his bed and supper at the same rate as marks. She has the rule cut on a board over the eastern hearth in the old strokes: Bonn no bathar, an aon bhobhla, coin or goods, the same bowl.

title: The carters of Doire chaol swear at Seònaid's table
summary: Through the winter some thirty carters of Doire chaol, Cuan chrom and the capital meet at the eastern hearth of An Taigh-seinnse Mòr over the lowered rate for hauling coal. On Pàdraig mac Artair's counsel they swear, with their hands on the board of Seònaid's rule, to go to Ros dhomhain together and haul nothing at the new rate.

title: Amos Tanner bargains with the carters at An Taigh-seinnse Mòr
summary: Amos Tanner, agent of A' Chompanaidh for the carriage of coal, rides up Rathad na Mèinne to meet the carters' guild of Doire chaol at An Taigh-seinnse Mòr. He tells them of the new coal stage at Seann Toll and the lesser hauling on the road, and they bargain over the rate into the night.
